newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Crowded Chinese ship in distress off Bermuda.
newsitem.headline: Crowded Chinese ship in distress off Bermuda.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard found a Chinese ship crowded with 109 people aboard drifting in the North Atlantic and will tow the vessel to Bermuda, the Bermudan government said on Saturday.

The cargo ship Xing Da is suspected of trying to smuggle illegal migrants into the United States, a statement issued by Bermuda's Minister of Labor, Home Affairs and Public Safety, Quinton Edness, said.
The 83 passengers and 26 crew have been aboard the ship since June and were found dehydrated, the statement.
The U.S. Coast Guard has flown water to the ship located 110 miles (177 km) off Bermuda and will tow the crippled ship to the British island.
In Washington, the U.S. Coast Guard confirmed that the Xing Da was adrift in six-foot (two-metre) swells, but gave no further details.
"We have an ongoing search and rescue operation for a vessel that is in distress north of Bermuda," spokesman Lieutenant Gary Bracken said.
The official said he did not know whether the ship had already been taken under tow or whether the U.S. Coast Guard would wait until dawn to start the operation.

The Bermudan government said it had agreed to allow the ship to be brought into Bermuda waters on the condition that no one was allowed ashore and that the United States took charge of the people on board and the vessel.

"Because of the poor weather conditions, the inability of those aboard to repair the ship and the fact that there are not sufficient life rafts or life vests aboard, the situation is judged to have become dangerous," the statement said. "As a result, it is now being treated as a rescue operation."
